newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gas prices score slim gains on storage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gas prices score slim gains on storage.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices edged up slightly on Monday, buoyed by more storage buying despite that mild weather continued to undermine cooling demand, industry sources said.
But with hot weather fading and injections likely to taper next month as caverns fill, few expected much further upside in physical prices until heating loads kick in.
"The cash is stronger than people expected, but storage builds have to slow in October," said one Gulf Coast trader.
U.S. Gulf Coast prices firmed a couple of cents today to the high-$1.80s/mmBtu or better, 10 cents over Sept indices.
October Gulf gas was pegged between NYMEX plus two cents and NYMEX minus 10 cents.
Midcontinent pipes saw similar gains for swing to the mid-$1.70s, almost 10 cents over Sept 1 levels. October Midcon gas was offered at 18 cents under the screen.

In west Texas, El Paso Permian was up slightly to the mid-to-high $1.60s, five cents over index. South Texas gas also was slightly higher in the low-$1.80s, more than five cents over first of the month prices.
New York city gate swing gas was talked up a few cents to about $2.10, with October quoted at NYMEX plus 19 cents.
